title: Coherent lifting data compute an operation restriction fiber
statement:
Use spaces, homotopy fibers and coherent diagram spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the universes of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], and generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability]. Let $Q\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ be small with $Q_{[0]}$ and $Q_{[1]}$ spaces. Fix $k\geq1$, $C\in Q_{[k]}$, and its inert incidence diagram with edge projections $C_i$ and vertex projections $V_j$. Define $E_C$ to be the space of active arrows to $C$, allowing as source changes only equivalences over identity base arrows, with coherent triangles and all higher simplices; define $E_{C_i}$ in the same way. Let $R:E_C\to\prod_i E_{C_i}$ be restriction by inert block factorization. Fix active arrows $b_i:D_i\to C_i$, with $D_i\in Q_{[n_i]}$, and put $n=\sum_i n_i$. Let $\alpha:[n]\to[k]$ be the active arrow with $\alpha^{\mathrm{op}}(j)=\sum_{i\leq j}n_i$.

Define $L(b)$ to be the coherent space of the following data, allowing every object and every witness to vary. First choose endpoint factorizations of $D_i\xrightarrow{b_i}C_i\to V_{i-1},V_i$ through the inert first and last vertex projections of $D_i$; write the resulting arrows in $Q_{[0]}$ as $u_i^-,u_i^+$. Next choose junction equivalences $e_i:t(D_i)\to s(D_{i+1})$ and homotopies $u_{i+1}^-e_i\simeq u_i^+$. Next choose a source $D\in Q_{[n]}$ and inert block projections, equivalences of these blocks to the specified $D_i$, and their coherent identification with those junction data. The source projections, the $u_i^{\pm}$ and the junction homotopies define maps $D\to V_j$ and endpoint compatibility homotopies with the composites $D\to D_i\xrightarrow{b_i}C_i$. Finally choose a point in the homotopy fiber of the comparison of [lem-coef-operadic-block-incidence-lifting] over this compatible block-and-vertex datum. This last point consists of a map $a:D\to C$ over $\alpha$ and its coherent identification with that incidence datum. The definition of $L(b)$ retains transformations between all these data and every higher simplex, rather than only isomorphism classes or components.

Composing the final incidence identifications with the block equivalences gives a natural equivalence
$$L(b)\simeq\operatorname{hofib}_{b}(R).$$
It is compatible with restriction in arbitrary simplicial parameter spaces. The assertion includes $n_i=0$ and non-discrete $Q_{[0]}$, and makes no contractibility assertion about $L(b)$.

source.place: Definitions 2.4.1 and 3.1.13(i),(iii); agent-expanded comparison in the product assertion of the Erratum proof of Corollary E.0.1. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-operadic comparison. Identification of the full homotopy fiber with the endpoint/junction/source/incidence lifting groupoid, including parameter simplices.

proof.text: Write $F_b=\operatorname{hofib}_b(R)$. By the path-fiber definition, its datum is $(a:D\to C,h)$, where $h$ is a path from the tuple of restricted operations to $b$. A path in each operation groupoid consists of an equivalence $v_i:D|_i\simeq D_i$ over the identity and its triangle $b_iv_i\simeq a|_i$, with all higher data. These equivalences force the block arities to be $n_i$. If $\gamma:[m]\to[k]$ is the base of $a$, active means $\gamma^{\mathrm{op}}(0)=0$ and $\gamma^{\mathrm{op}}(k)=m$. Its consecutive differences are therefore $n_i$, so $m=n$ and $\gamma=\alpha$. This argument uses the identity-base restriction on source changes; allowing arbitrary active source maps would not give this fiber.

source.place: Erratum before Corollary E.0.1, corrected operation groupoid; explicit path-fiber and arity calculation.

proof.text: For any fixed source $D$ occurring in $F_b$, add its cocartesian inert block and vertex projections and their incidence triangles. They exist by the inert-lift axiom. Composite projections are cocartesian by the composition clause of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality]. Each alternative lift is initial in the corresponding lift category, so the space of its comparisons with a fixed lift, including the triangle, is contractible. The initial-object clause of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes the whole space of initial lifts contractible. Thus choosing a whole incidence projection diagram adds contractible coherent choices: choose its arrows and compare each composite to the direct lift in its initial-lift category. For parameter families use [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] on the pullback of $Q$ to the subcategory of inert base maps. That pullback is an inner fibration with every required lift, by the inert-lift axiom; its universal mapping squares are the restrictions of those in $Q$. The cited theorem supplies coherent lifts for every small parameter shape and compatible composites. No cocartesian lift of an active base arrow is assumed.

source.place: Definitions 2.4.1(i), 3.1.13(i); explicit use of cocartesian initial-lift and diagram transport tools.

proof.text: For a chosen inert edge $q:X\to Y$ and a prescribed map $g:X\to Z$ whose base factors through $p(q)$, the space of factorizations $(f:Y\to Z,fq\simeq g)$ over that specified base factorization is contractible. Indeed, the cocartesian mapping square of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] identifies the upper-left mapping space with the path pullback of the other three corners. Fixing $g$ and the base factor gives a homotopy fiber of an equivalence, equivalently the path space with fixed final endpoint, which contracts by shortening the path. Applying this to the first and last vertex projections of each $D_i$ gives the endpoint maps $u_i^\pm$ and their factorization witnesses, with contractible choices. This remains true for $n_i=0$: use the same identity vertex projection twice, retaining both prescribed endpoint witnesses rather than identifying or discarding them.

source.place: Definitions 2.4.1(i), 3.1.13(i); endpoint factorization via the cocartesian mapping-space universal property.

proof.text: Keep $(a,h)$ and these choices fixed. For each source vertex $t_j$, composing $a$ with $C\to V_j$ and factoring through $D\to D(t_j)$ gives a map $w_j:D(t_j)\to V_j$. For each incidence $j=i-1,i$, factor the block equivalence $v_i$ through the corresponding source endpoint projection. This gives an equivalence $r_i^\pm:D(t_j)\to s(D_i),t(D_i)$, together with its triangle. The comparison is invertible because both projections are cocartesian lifts of the same inert map after the equivalence $v_i$; their initial-lift comparison is an equivalence. Factoring the endpoint of $h_i$ gives $u_i^\pm r_i^\pm\simeq w_j$. All these are factorizations of specified composites, so the mapping-square argument of step 3 gives contractible choices of their triangles as well. At a junction the common object is $D(t_i)$, even when several $t_i$ coincide. This identifies the common-source endpoint description without imposing an equality of endpoints in $Q_{[0]}$.

source.place: Definitions 2.4.1(i),(iii), 3.1.13; endpoint restrictions of the fixed operation-path triangle.

proof.text: The junction data are obtained by replacing the two comparisons from the common vertex with one comparison between their targets. More explicitly, $e_i:t(D_i)\to s(D_{i+1})$ is specified together with $e_i r_i^+\simeq r_{i+1}^-$; composition with the endpoint triangles gives $u_{i+1}^-e_i\simeq u_i^+$. There is a contractible space of such comparisons with the displayed witness, since both endpoint lifts are initial in the same lift category of step 4. This is exactly the junction together with its coherent identification required in $L(b)$. The endpoint homotopy is induced by those retained triangles; it is not an additional independently chosen loop at $V_i$. The source part of $L(b)$ is the same $D$, its block projections and $v_i$, now written with these junctions. Consequently this operation neither reconstructs a new source from its components nor invokes the Segal-product theorem that cites the present item.

source.place: Erratum proof of E.0.1, expansion of the product comparison; explicit common-vertex junction comparison.

proof.text: The maps $w_j$, block maps $b_iv_i$ and endpoint triangles of steps 3-5 are a point $z$ of the incidence homotopy limit for $D,C,\alpha$. Retaining $a$ and its identification with $z$ is exactly the last homotopy-fiber datum in $L(b)$, by [lem-coef-operadic-block-incidence-lifting]. Its statement includes coherence in source equivalences and projection diagrams, so it applies also when $D$ varies along a triangle in the operation space. In using this presentation, a homotopy in the incidence limit comprises its edge, vertex and compatibility coordinates together. Hence the restriction identification in $F_b$ is its edge part; the other coordinates are precisely the factorizations just added. No second independent incidence homotopy is appended to the same data. We do not forget $a$ or replace its last homotopy fiber by a point.

source.place: Definitions 2.4.1(iii), 3.1.13(iii); fixed-source block-incidence comparison, reorganized with its full homotopy-fiber coordinates.

proof.text: Let $\widehat F_b$ be the coherent space of $(a,h)\in F_b$ together with the projection diagrams, endpoint factorizations, vertex comparisons and their composition witnesses just specified. Reading its data in the order endpoint, junction, source, incidence gives the data defining $L(b)$. Reading a point of $L(b)$ in reverse order gives $a$ and, by composing its incidence edge identification with the specified block equivalences, the path $h:R(a)\to b$. Its retained source/junction identifications supply the vertex comparisons of step 4. The two readings preserve every witness; the triangular identifications of factorizations are the comparisons from the same initial-lift categories. Their composites are identified with the original triangles by the contractible comparison spaces in steps 2-5. This gives inverse coherent equivalences $L(b)\simeq\widehat F_b$. In particular it compares full diagram spaces, not their components.

source.place: Agent expansion of the operation-groupoid fiber in the product assertion of the Erratum proof of E.0.1.

proof.text: The forgetful map $p:\widehat F_b\to F_b$ removes only the auxiliary factorization and comparison data. For each fixed $(a,h)$, steps 2-5 give a finite succession of contractible choice spaces: inert lifts, factorizations of specified endpoint maps, and comparisons of the endpoint lifts with fixed source vertices. These assertions concern homotopy fibers with their identification with $(a,h)$ retained. For each forgetful map $f:A\to B$, apply [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] with $u=r=f$ and $q=v=\operatorname{id}_B$. Every fiber map goes from the contractible choice space to the contractible homotopy fiber of the identity. Thus each forgetful map is an equivalence, and so is $p$. The spaces are Kan: use cores of the coherent diagram categories and the Kan-core clause of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Composing step 7 with $p$ proves the asserted equivalence, whose forward map is the one specified in the statement.

source.place: Erratum proof of E.0.1; homotopy-fiber test applied only to auxiliary choices over a fixed operation and restriction path.

proof.text: For a simplicial map $K\to K\prime$, restriction of a coherent family precomposes every coordinate $K\prime\times\Delta^m\to Q$ by $K\times\Delta^m\to K\prime\times\Delta^m$. It commutes with every source, block, endpoint and incidence restriction and with the composition of their triangle witnesses. Thus the two readings in step 7 and the forgetful map in step 8 commute with parameter restriction. Step 2 supplies the coherent choices in families, so no independently selected inverse at individual vertices is used. Zero-length blocks have the identity endpoint projection; repeated partial sums leave the common-source-vertex argument unchanged. No discreteness of $Q_{[0]}$ was used: its paths and every junction witness were retained. The contraction in step 8 takes place over each fixed $(a,h)$, so it makes no assertion that $F_b$ or $L(b)$ itself is contractible.
